sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Every department already has the geography. It is in forty different files. Boundaries, operational layers, road shapefiles and survey sheets each sit in their own folder and their own format, converted by hand whenever someone needs a map.

The problem

Scattered GIS assets

Boundaries, operational layers and survey sheets each sit in their own format, converted by hand on demand.

Now · one catalog, one map, one composition

Road networks too big for a browser

A single state's road network can exceed 150,000 segments. Sent as one file it stalls the browser, so planning a route on the real network is not practical.

Now · served by map area, or as tiles

Field teams need offline

A district team going out needs a printed sheet and something a handheld can open — not a web page they cannot reach once they leave coverage.

Now · atlas sheets and field map packages

The habit it turns on

Pick the layers that matter, save the composition, work from it. That is the pair of actions an operator repeats all day, at whatever level their jurisdiction starts — nation, state, district, sub-district or village.

Administrative boundariesBeats & jurisdictions Crime hotspotsCCTV nodes Offender layersGeo-fences Patrol routesEvent & deployment planning

Deploying in a new state · the platform does not change, six things do

Administrative boundaries

The state's own authoritative state, district, sub-district and village layers replace the base set.

Jurisdiction hierarchy and names

Mandal, taluk, tehsil, block, circle — the levels and their labels are set to match how the state is actually administered.

Road network

The state's network is loaded into the spatial database and served by map area, so size stops being a limit.

Operational layers

The department's own enforcement, asset or incident layers are converted and added to the catalog.

Identity and roles

Connected to the department's existing identity provider, with the role-to-workspace matrix set to its own rank structure.

Language

Interface labels and map annotation in the languages the department works in.

None of the six requires a code change. The map engine, catalog and composition model, routing, field products, serving strategy and audit model are identical across deployments — which is why a second state costs a fraction of the first.

sections.title: Safeguards
sections.html:
Safeguards

What it will not do, and what it always keeps.

  • Authorisation enforced on the server as well as in the interface.
  • Every action recorded in an exportable trail.
  • Each layer carries the pipeline it came from, so its currency and reliability are visible.
